title: Bible Translation
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 7 Christian Religious Education; not yet checked by a CRE teacher; not loaded by the live tutor

skills.key_step: The learner identifies versions used today (such as the Good News Bible, New International Version, King James, Biblia Habari Njema), discusses why the Bible was translated, describes translation from Hebrew, Aramaic and Greek into local languages, and examines its social and economic effects (literacy, written languages, schools, printing jobs).

floor.prerequisite: Knows why the Bible is translated into local languages.
floor.question: Name an advantage of a Bible in your own language.

representations: a chain: Hebrew and Greek, English, Kiswahili, local language
contexts: a church using a Kikuyu Bible

board.do: Draw a chain from Hebrew and Greek to a Kenyan language.

board.say: In which languages was the Bible first written?

board.do: Wait for the learner to say Hebrew, Aramaic and Greek.

misconceptions.ask: In which language was most of the New Testament first written?
misconceptions.repair: Write the three original languages: Hebrew (most of the Old Testament), Aramaic (parts), Greek (New Testament).

listen_for: To make the church leaders important
misconceptions.ask: Why is the Bible translated into Kenyan languages?
misconceptions.repair: Ask: who can read Greek? Translation is so everyone can read in their own language.

misconceptions.ask: Which is a social effect of translating the Bible into local languages?
misconceptions.repair: List effects: literacy, schools, written local languages, preserved culture, jobs in printing.

listen_for: A different Bible with a different message
misconceptions.repair: Read John 3:16 in two English versions: same meaning, different words.

checks.question: In which language was most of the New Testament first written?
Name a social effect of translation.
